Migrating copied database helpers to Panoptes

Source: vignettes/migrating-to-panoptes.Rmd
migrating-to-panoptes.Rmd

Migration boundary

The CohortGenerator prototype mixed reusable infrastructure with package-owned behavior. Migration moves declaration parsing, selection, environment policy, adapters, context assembly, resource lifecycle, and CI drift detection to Panoptes. It keeps cohort fixtures, generation calls, assertions, cohort tables, and cleanup in CohortGenerator.

Helper mapping

Copied helper concept Panoptes replacement
getDatabaseTestConfig() readDatabaseTestConfig()
getSelectedTestDbms() getSelectedTestDbms(config)
getDatabasePlatformConfig() getDatabasePlatformConfig(config)
per-DBMS environment functions resolveDatabaseTestEnvironment() plus aliases
validateDatabaseTestEnvironment() same public name with required/optional policy
per-DBMS connection functions internal Panoptes adapters
getDatabaseTestContext() createDatabaseTestContext()
getPlatformConnectionDetails() withDatabaseTestContext()
manual unique cohort table suffix context$objectPrefix or createUniqueDatabaseObjectName()
global SqlRender option assignment scoped automatically by withDatabaseTestContext()
BigQuery temporary file scoped automatically by withDatabaseTestContext()
hard-coded workflow matrix getDatabaseTestMatrix() and validateDatabaseTestWorkflow()

The generic tests from test-database-platforms.R move to Panoptes. Keep a small consumer integration test proving that the installed package declaration is found and that the package behavior test receives the expected context.

Update the declaration

The prototype’s environmentPrefix was descriptive and could not represent exceptions such as SQL Server’s repeated SERVER, Snowflake’s CDM53_SCHEMA, or BigQuery’s prefix. Panoptes rejects that field. Remove it and map existing secrets to normalized HADES_* variables in the workflow, or pass explicit aliases while migrating.

Add these executable fields to every platform:

  • runner: the GitHub runner label;
  • os: any, linux, windows, or macos; and
  • githubEnvironment: the protected GitHub environment name.

The template puts BigQuery on windows-latest, resolving the prototype’s Windows-only helper versus Ubuntu-only matrix conflict.

Replace orchestration

Replace this ordering from the prototype:

construct context -> validate environment -> download drivers -> set option

with:

config <- Panoptes::readDatabaseTestConfig(package = "CohortGenerator")
Panoptes::skipIfNoLiveDatabase(config)

Panoptes::withDatabaseTestContext(
  config,
  legacyAliases = cohortGeneratorAliases,
  verify = TRUE,
  {
    # Existing CohortGenerator behavior and on.exit() table cleanup.
  }
)

Panoptes validates before it calls DatabaseConnector and does not download JDBC drivers. Driver installation belongs in CI setup or a developer’s configured driver folder, avoiding network activity during context validation.

Update CI

Map existing secrets to the normalized variables inside each matrix job. Split the current all-platform pull-request matrix into the declared tiers:

  • PostgreSQL, SQL Server, and Oracle on pull-request;
  • Redshift, Spark, BigQuery, Snowflake, and IRIS on scheduled;
  • BigQuery on its declared Windows runner.

Add workflow-validation tests for each static matrix. Keep secrets out of the ordinary check workflow. Pin Panoptes to a released tag before broad adoption.

Remove copied code only after the integration passes

Once the package behavior test passes through Panoptes:

  1. remove copied configuration, environment, and adapter helpers;
  2. remove generic helper unit tests now covered by Panoptes;
  3. retain the consumer behavior test and cleanup;
  4. retain a declaration-discovery integration test; and
  5. run at least one required and one scheduled external platform before the migration is considered complete.
